listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Thursday, October 29. Our lead story is from Spain. The country is dealing with its second deadly high-speed rail crash this year. One train struck another from behind, and sixty-eight people were killed. The crash has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the rail network. It comes ahead of a national election in Spain. Now the front page. GitHub announced its twenty twenty-six Octoverse report at its Universe event. Simon Willison, who attended, says the numbers show the impact of agentic engineering. In sports, the Houston Rockets stayed unbeaten. They beat the Milwaukee Bucks one hundred thirty-two to one hundred. Fred VanVleet scored twenty-four points and Amen Thompson added twenty-three. In politics, a judge denied the Justice Department's bid to stop processing California ballots. The federal government has already filed notice that it will appeal. Also, a hacktivist group says it exposed the identities of more than forty thousand Department of Homeland Security employees. The group says the government's lack of transparency made it fair play. Now the sections. In tech, a Hacker News post claims Claude Code regularly sends each background agent's transcript to its model. It drew a lot of discussion. Simon Willison also writes that October is an inflection point for vibe game development. In politics, The Lever reports that the Democratic left is betting it can win more by working with the House Speaker. NPR reports that three new polls show support for President Trump falling among white evangelicals. In world news, Flavio Bolsonaro, the defeated Brazilian candidate, arrived in Miami after authorities ordered him to surrender his passport. El Salvador is sending two thousand troops to Haiti to recover four missing soldiers. In sports, Christian McCaffrey may have a hamstring issue during the 49ers' bye week. Alexander Volkanovski jumps in ESPN's pound-for-pound rankings at age thirty-eight. The Rockets, now five and oh, face the Mavericks on Friday. In Atlanta, Alpharetta's Ronara Villas project continues the push toward density. A retail overhaul has begun on a historic Virginia-Highland strip. A forty-mile Flint Riverway trail concept is gaining momentum. In architecture, Allplan Max brings engineering AI across its portfolio. Chaos is adding live BIM data insights to Enscape. David Baker Architects completed fifty-nine affordable homes in Oakland. In science, the Artemis Three core stage has been joined with its boosters at Kennedy Space Center. A new estimate suggests seventy-five percent of NFL players may develop CTE. And new marine protected areas in Pemba show the value of collaboration. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Spain reckons with 2nd deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election
lead.note: Spain is dealing with its second high-speed rail disaster this year. In the latest crash, one train struck another from behind, and 68 people were killed. The accident has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network. It comes ahead of a national election, so the question of rail safety arrives at a politically sensitive moment. For a reader who follows engineering and infrastructure, the story is a reminder of how much depends on the systems that keep large transport networks running safely. The summary does not give a cause, so the established facts are the death toll, the type of collision, and the fact that this is the second major crash of the year. Further reporting should show what investigators find and how officials respond.
